newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-ALONSO TO MEET DEWULF IN FIRST ATP TOUR FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ALONSO TO MEET DEWULF IN FIRST ATP TOUR FINAL.

text.p: Spain's Julian Alonso reached his first ATP Tour final at only his third attempt when he beat Czech Slava Dosedel 6-3 6-4 at the Generali Open on Saturday.
In Sunday's final, 19-year-old Alonso will meet 10th-seeded Belgian and French Open semifinalist Filip Dewulf, who had little trouble defeating Spaniard Galo Blanco 6-3 6-2.

Alonso's success was the biggest surprise of the $535,000 clay court tournament, which lost top seeds Thomas Muster, Yevgeny Kafelnikov, Alex Corretja and French Open champion Gustavo Kuerten in earlier rounds.
"The top players have had a tough time reaching finals lately. This has been typical all year," said Dewulf.
This week, Alonso achieved his best world ranking of 92, giving Spain a record 15 players in the top 100.

Earlier this year, he made the third round at Key Biscayne by defeating Steve Bryan and Tim Henman and the second round in Barcelona. He also won two challenger tournaments in Venice and Contrexville.
"I didn't think I could make it this far, but I improved from match to match and now I think I could even win this tournament," said Alonso.
"I don't care who my next opponent is. When I am on the court I am at war with myself and not my opponent."
Alonso, sponsored and managed by former leading Spanish player Emilio Sanchez, took a quick 5-1 lead in the first set before his form wavered slightly and he dropped serve at 5-2.
But he quickly recuperated, re-broke and took the set on serve before beginning the second set with a break.
Although 15th-seeded Dosedel stepped up a gear and broke for 2-2, he was unable to match Alonso's pace. Dosedel lost his serve at 4-3 and three games later was out.
Dewulf, who recorded his only tournament win at the 1995 hard court CA-Trophy in Vienna, had an easier task against French Open quarter-finalist Blanco.
The Belgian, who has not lost a set here, needed a single break at 2-0 to take the first set, and breaks at 1-0 and 5-2 to enter his first final of 1997.
"I think he must have been a bit injured today. He wasn't as aggressive and fresh as in previous matches," Dewulf said about Blanco who eliminated world number four Corretja in round three.
"My only other victory was in Austria. I must like the air here," he added. "The country where you score your first win becomes special and you like to return."
